questions.q: Why can a `PyTorchJob` show status `Running` even when something is actually wrong?
options: PyTorchJob status is purely cosmetic and never reflects real state
The Training Operator reports the job's overall lifecycle condition, which is a different layer from individual pod health underneath it
Running always means every pod is healthy by definition
Kubernetes does not track job status at all
questions.explain: Job-level status and pod-level status answer different questions — a job can show Running while one of its worker pods is in CrashLoopBackOff, so both layers need checking.

questions.q: What is the Kubeflow Central Dashboard primarily used for?
options: Compiling CUDA kernels
As the web UI entry point researchers use to navigate notebooks, pipelines, and training tooling
Allocating GPU cost across namespaces
Replacing kubectl entirely for all cluster operations
questions.explain: The Central Dashboard is where researchers typically start when checking on their work, before drilling into a specific tool like TensorBoard or a notebook.

questions.q: What makes it possible to pull logs from all 64 worker pods of a PyTorchJob with a single `kubectl logs` command?
options: Kubernetes automatically merges logs from every pod in a namespace
A label (set automatically by the Training Operator on every pod in the job) that a label selector can target in one query
All 64 pods share a single container
Logs are stored in a central database instead of per-pod
questions.explain: The Training Operator labels every pod belonging to a job (e.g. with the job name), so a label-selector query against that label targets all of them in one command.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat loss-curve observability (via TensorBoard) as a separate concern from infrastructure metrics like GPU utilization?
options: Because TensorBoard and GPU metrics measure the exact same thing
Because a job can be Running with fully utilized GPUs while the model is still training on a diverging loss — infrastructure health doesn't guarantee training health
Because TensorBoard replaces the need for DCGM metrics
Because loss curves are only relevant after training completes
questions.explain: Infrastructure observability (is the hardware working) and training observability (is the model actually learning) are genuinely separate questions, and a dashboard answering one doesn't answer the other.

questions.q: What is a PyTorchJob's status condition sequence, as tracked by the Training Operator?
options: Created -> Running -> (Succeeded | Failed)
Pending -> Scheduled -> Terminated, with no other states
Only Running or Stopped, with no intermediate states
Queued -> Billed -> Archived
questions.explain: The Training Operator tracks a PyTorchJob through Created, then Running, then a terminal state of either Succeeded or Failed.
